links.outcome: Expert-rated quality of LLM discharge reports versus human-authored reports on same cases
links.effect: Friedman χ2(3)=23.93, p<0.001; human reports scored significantly lower than SP (p=0.003), SBP (p=0.003), SBP+W (p=0.025) after Bonferroni correction.
links.quote: Post hoc pairwise comparisons using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction showed that Strategy A yielded significantly lower scores than Strategy B ( p = 0.003), Strategy C ( p = 0.003), and Strategy D ( p = 0.025).

links.outcome: Inter-rater agreement between blinded physician raters on quality scores
links.effect: Quadratic weighted kappa 0.354 (95% CI 0.15–0.53), fair agreement; strategy-level kappas lower with wide CIs.
links.quote: Quadratic weighted Cohen’s kappa (see Table 7 ) indicated fair overall agreement (κ = 0.354; 95% CI 0.15– 0.53).

links.outcome: Phrase-level hallucination rate in AI-generated and human discharge reports
links.effect: Overall 9.0% (107/1190) hallucinated phrases; SBP 1.4%, SP 6.3%, SBP+W 11.1%, human-authored 22.6%.
links.quote: Overall, 71.3% (849/1190) of phrases were classified as containing no hallucinations, 19.7% (234/1190) as deductions, and 9.0% (107/1190) as hallucinations.

links.outcome: Comparison of prompt architectures (single vs section-based vs refinement) on expert-rated quality
links.effect: Prompting strategies differed from human reports but no significant differences among SP, SBP, SBP+W after correction; SBP had highest median and largest regression effect.
links.quote: In contrast, we found no statistically significant differences among Strategies B, C, and D after correction (see Table 5 ).
